documents.title: Cranberry pills?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Random question - my mom swears by cranberry pills for bladder infections. Since I've had two, should I be taking them? No symptoms right now, just wondering.

documents.title: RE: Cranberry pills?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. The research on cranberry is mixed - some studies show a small benefit for women who get frequent infections, others show nothing. You've had two, months apart, and you're doing all the right things, so I wouldn't push it. If you want to try it, it's very unlikely to hurt, but let me know so I can put it on your list. The water and voiding habits matter more.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 25 y/o.

Feeling well. No urinary symptoms since last October - two cystitis episodes total (2/2025, 10/2025), both nitrofurantoin-responsive, culture last time E. coli. Didn't start cranberry. Constipation quiet; psyllium a few times a month. Still full-time at the bakery.

Meds: psyllium PRN, multivitamin with zinc daily. NKDA.
Never smoker; 1-2 drinks on weekends.

Exam: vitals normal. Well-appearing young woman. HEENT clear. Neck without adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular rate and rhythm. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin without lesions of concern.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
- Cervical screening due (Pap 8/2023 normal). She'd rather not do it today - prefers a dedicated visit; will book for September and do her flu shot then.
- Labs: CBC/CMP normal last summer; nothing needed this year.
- Functional constipation: stable.
- Hx cystitis x2: no recurrence. Reviewed prevention habits.
Next physical summer 2027.

documents.title: Appointment Scheduled

documents.body: At checkout: booked Pap + flu vaccine visit with PCP Thu 9/17 at 3:30 (after her shift). Flu supply expected by then. Reminder will go out the week before.
